title: Turn every field into a flag
prompt: Write the mapped type `Flags<T>`: an object with the same keys as `T`, where every field is a `boolean`. Then write `allOff<T extends object>(obj: T): Flags<T>` that returns an object with every key of `obj` set to `false`.
hints: `{ [K in keyof T]: ... }` makes one field per key of `T`.
Every field is `boolean`, whatever its type was in `T`.
At runtime, loop over `Object.keys(obj)` and set each key to `false`.
checks: __same(allOff({ email: "a@b.c", age: 3 }), { email: false, age: false })
typeChecks: __Equal<Flags<{ email: string; age: number }>, { email: boolean; age: boolean }>
rejects: const f: Flags<{ a: string }> = { a: "yes" }

wrongAnswers.misconception: Adds `?`, so every flag is optional and `allOff` can return `{}`.
Uses `Record<string, boolean>`, which allows any key.

feedback: `{ [K in keyof T]: ... }` makes one field per key of `T`.
